title: PingFederate LAB: the features behind AI agents

glossary.definition: An authorization request with response_mode=pi.flow. PingFederate answers with a JSON flow instead of a login page, and the app posts the user's answers to it until the flow says COMPLETED. PingFederate still decides who may sign in.
Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636). The client sends a hash of a secret it created when it starts a sign-in and the secret itself when it redeems the code, so a stolen code is useless on its own.
Pushed Authorization Request (RFC 9126). The client sends the authorization request straight to the server and gets back a short reference, so the request cannot be read or changed in the browser.
Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396). The request carries structured authorization_details, for example one transfer of an exact amount between two accounts, instead of a broad scope.
Demonstrating Proof of Possession (RFC 9449). The token is bound to a key the client holds, and each call carries a signed proof, so a copied token does not work on its own.
Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication. The app asks for a sign-in for a named user, and the user approves on another device; the app polls for the result.
RFC 7591 and RFC 7592. A client registers itself with the authorization server, using a one-time initial access token, and can manage or delete its own registration.
RFC 8693. A client sends one token and gets a different one back, for example a token for an agent acting for the user, with an act claim naming the actor.
A claim in an exchanged token that names who is acting on behalf of the subject. Nested act claims show a chain of actors.
An OpenID Connect endpoint that returns claims about the signed-in user when called with the user's access token.
Mock runs every card against a simulated PingFederate inside the lab, offline. Live sends every call to the PingFederate named in Settings, and only to that one address.

cards.label: Start the lab and check it
cards.description: Run npm start, then npm run doctor in another terminal. Mock mode needs no settings.

cards.label: Choose mock or live
cards.description: The header toggle switches the whole lab. Live needs a PingFederate issuer and the client settings in Settings.

cards.label: Sign in with pi.flow
cards.description: Open a flow, post a username and password, and read the code PingFederate returns.

cards.label: Register and delete a client
cards.description: Four steps: initial access token, register, use, delete.

cards.label: Authorize one exact transfer
cards.description: RAR sent through PAR, with an optional DPoP-bound token.

cards.label: Approve a request on another device
cards.description: Start a CIBA request for a named user and approve it on the lab's approve step.

cards.label: Bind a token to a key
cards.description: Sign in with DPoP and read the proof the client sends.

cards.label: Exchange a token twice
cards.description: User token to agent token to MCP token; read the act claim at each hop.

cards.label: Read the user's claims
cards.description: Call the Userinfo endpoint with the signed-in user's access token.

cards.label: Change a parameter and compare
cards.description: Pick a protocol, change one parameter, run it, and compare the traces.

cards.label: PKCE and PAR, the building blocks
cards.description: The authorization-code flow with a code challenge, then the same request pushed.
